title: Banner, backdrops & flags · Vertical banner artwork
slide_intent: Allocate a stable identifier area and an adaptable lower field on a tall sign. Viewers can recognize the program from a distance before reading details or studying a photograph.
strategic_value: A fixed curve and program mark can give Special Olympics banners a family resemblance across venues with different proportions.
demonstration: Two main banners reverse the red and white treatment. A third fills the lower field with an athlete photograph. Short and long blue extension diagrams isolate the variable portion.
practical_value: Choose the white- or red-ground mark, then fit a web address, partner marks or a photograph beneath the curve. Change the lower area to suit the venue.

content_islands.name: Adaptation instructions
content_islands.spec: At left identify the program-name substitution and the uses for the remaining banner field.

content_islands.name: Two colorways and image option
content_islands.spec: Show tall red and white examples with the same mark relationship to the curve. Beside them place a photographed example whose image meets the curve.

content_islands.name: Proportion diagrams
content_islands.spec: At far right show a short and a tall outline with the header held fixed. Use vertical arrows to identify the adjustable area.
